newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican overnight Cetes rates close down.
newsitem.headline: Mexican overnight Cetes rates close down.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 25 basis points at 24.25 percent on expectations primary rates would fall later in the day.
"Although turnover has been light, liquidity is still ample, with foreign investors stepping in and money flowing back after the weekend," a trader said.
"Furthermore, as primary rates look like falling, it's best to buy now," he added.
A Reuters survey showed an average forecast assignment of 24.78 percent for the bellwether 28-day Cetes at the primary auction, or 93 basis points below last week's rate.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 15 basis points at 25.35 percent.
Traders noted government overnight rates closed above a session low of 23.65 percent on profit-taking.
Foreign traders entering the money market were cited as one reason 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.8340/7.8380 per dollar, dealers said.
A reflection of ample liquidity in the system was Banco de Mexico's relatively light liquidity injection of 1.218 billion pesos, which it assigned as an overnight credit at 25.35 percent.
Dealers said further falls in secondary rates could be thwarted by December inflation figures, due out on Thursday. ((--Patricia Lezama, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9554))
